688	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
689	
690	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
691	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
692	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
693	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
694	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
695	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
696	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
697	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
698	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
699	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
700	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
701	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
702	
703	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
704	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
705	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
706	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is
707	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
708	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
709	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
710	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
711	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
712	are the supported alternative.

716	## 8. Command inventory, outputs and parity (AR-13 surfaces, AR-16)
717	
718	`workflows/command-inventory.v1.json` is the candidate single inventory,
719	validated by `command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
720	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
721	
722	| Group | Commands |

Store migrate/rollback use the same installation transition protocol (security S7); their command authorization class is `core-transition-leases`.
1118	
1119	Explicit CLI workspace roots may normalize one terminal slash before constructing canonical configuration. Config2 itself contains strict logical paths (plus `.` root sentinel); malformed Config2 is rejected before either discovery instrument. The custody instrument's synthetic direct inputs exercise this CLI normalization and do not bypass Config2 schema admission.
1120	
1121	Test-step admission validates the complete closed TestExecutionStepParams before any nested access and requires consentSource to equal the actual admitted security grant projection (`interactive-explicit` -> `interactive-consent`, policy-record -> pre-existing-policy). A caller cannot relabel interactive consent as policy consent for CI. Live source movement in a test step has TEST.SOURCE_MOVED, separately from repair's condition. Intake imports become analysis inputs only through the identity contract's retained source-correspondence join.
1122	
1123	The public-detail registry separates public records from internal decision aliases. Host projection always emits PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT for the shared discovery cap (security, shared-helper and native paths) and PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID for malformed explicit roots; diagnostic counts/reasons travel in subject. Internal WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT, native.too-many-units and native.explicit-root-grammar are never public enum values. The native table key provider-unavailable/capability-missing projects as native.capability-unavailable. The removed pre-Plan projection refusal is retired with no alias. Thus the same shared condition has one machine detail code independent of the instrument that detected it.
1124	
1125	Recovery in a later invocation uses the security S10.2 RepairRecoveryAuthorizationV1 and the closed RepairRecoveryIntentV1 retained by its mutation step. The host validates the original journal/plan, admits the fresh authorization and passes a trusted projection to the recovery mechanics; the journal retains the full security.repair-recovery-authorization.v1 reference. The observed journal-state digest prevents a grant from authorizing a changed recovery state. Immediate compensating rollback inside a still-running admitted apply attempt remains part of that apply's broker authority (including cleanup after revocation); it does not fabricate a fresh recovery authorization. The same guarded preimage/postimage mechanics serve both paths, and no public request can invoke those mechanics without admission.
1126	
1127	
1128	Installation operations (all five core/store operations) retain the same closed intent through mutation inputDescriptorDigest. Security S9.2 owns InstallationTransitionJournalV1. Each durable revision is addressed by the full H('security.installation-transition-journal.v1', revision) reference; its state changes therefore produce a new reference. The installation journal location under the fence selects the current revision, never a caller-supplied reference. An initial mutation Attempt retains installationJournalRefs in durable write order, including failed or abandoned attempts; no field is present if no journal was written. Its first revision is LEASED after the complete derived lock set was acquired. A fresh recovery Attempt instead retains installationRecoveryStartRef, exactly the current revision observed under the fence; its installationJournalRefs begin with that observed revision and then contain the new durable revisions written by this attempt. That first observation is not falsely counted as a write by the recovering attempt. This is operational custody evidence, excluded from Run identity. A host validates each reference/preimage and its intentDigest against the step before retaining it. On crash, journal recovery is the first action under the next installation fence, before project admission. It revalidates the closed intent, recomputes its digest and derived lease set over the frozen registry, and rejects mismatches before interpreting the recovery table. A self-consistent hash cannot make an invalid lease scope lawful.
1129	
1130	Journal revision order is LEASED → PREPARING → PREPARED → COMMITTED → DONE, or ABORTED from a precommit state. A recovery that determines RESUME-COMMIT from the store footprint first retains COMMITTED if needed, then DONE; it never rewrites history to imply an unobserved earlier commit. The host binds the frozen intent and immutable registry/scope fields across every retained revision.
1131	
1132	
1133	Before ordinary project admission, the host inserts a required installation-recovery mutation step if the fenced installation journal requires recovery. It uses the journal's original operation and retained CoreTransitionIntentV1 as inputDescriptorDigest, and a fresh host-minted RequestId/ExecutionId for the recovery invocation/attempt. The built-in workflow name is the originating installation command (from the closed command inventory); this is a host-started recovery invocation, not a second execution of that command's update recipe or an implicit mutation retry. Only the already-journaled transition may be completed or aborted through S9.2; caller parameters cannot nominate an installationRecoveryStartRef or grant extra effects. If recovery fails or is busy, ordinary project admission does not proceed. Terminal DONE/ABORTED journals need release/cleanup only. The new attempt links to the observed durable revision and never appends fictional writes to or rewrites an earlier abandoned Attempt. A recovery segment may begin in any closed state; it must bind that starting reference, retain the same admitted intent/registry/scope, and follow the state table. This gives PREPARED→COMMITTED→DONE recovery a representable independent history while the original attempt remains LEASED→PREPARING→PREPARED.
1134	
1135	
1136	There is one explicit consent mapping, applied only after actual security admission:
1137	
1138	| Security consent.mode | TestExecutionStepParams.consentSource | RepairApplyParams.consentSource |
1139	|---|---|---|
1140	| interactive-explicit | interactive-consent | interactive |
1141	| policy-record | pre-existing-policy | policy |
1142	
1143	These field-specific spellings do not define independent authorization mechanisms. Test and repair projections carry the mapped source, and repair additionally carries the admitted CI observation; their workflow mechanics require exact equality with the selected step/context. Interactive consent refuses in CI at security admission. Policy-record consent is valid both in CI and outside CI when the actual policy admission succeeds. Relabelling an admitted grant's source is refused. A completed idempotent repair replay performs no mutation; it returns the existing receipt under the existing replay contract.

56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are
123	discovered **automatically** for the zero-config full product, with precedence:
124	
125	| Source | Provenance `unitSource` | Custody failure |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| repeatable CLI `--workspace-root PATH` overrides | `explicit-joins` | refuses (explicit intent) |
128	| admitted Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots` (foundation product-configuration schema v2) | `config-workspace-roots` | refuses |
129	| marker scan of the admitted root | `automatic` | unit excluded, recorded in `excludedUnits` with the reason |
130	
131	An explicit source suppresses automatic discovery. Every directory from the
132	root to a unit must pass directory custody and stay inside the root (no
133	absolute, `.`, `..`, backslash or NUL segments); every marker file must pass
134	file custody. A manifest is **data**: discovery records its presence and later
135	readers parse it as data only, never running scripts, hooks, plugins or
136	workspace globs and never writing source.
137	
138	**One shared discovery rule (MUST-3).** The zero-config rule is stated once, in
139	`docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by this
140	instrument and by the native unit instrument (native §1.4); neither restates
141	it. Before any custody walk, automatic discovery prunes, by **exact path

145	source directory merely called `target`, such as `packages/target` or
146	`src/target`, is ordinary source). A pruned tree yields no unit, no marker,
147	no custody walk and no program member; its anchor is recorded **once** in

154	`discovery-prunes-installed-dependencies-and-refuses-real-cap-typed`: 4200

159	`discovery.workspaceRoots` values are normalized by the shared

168	absolute, backslash or NUL segment is `JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`. An explicit root
169	inside a pruned tree refuses `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE:<reason>:<anchor>`. An
170	explicit root **without a language marker** is admitted here for custody (unit

172	`EXPLICIT_ROOT_WITHOUT_LANGUAGE_MARKER:<path>`) and refused by the language-unit
173	layer as `CONFIG.INVALID` / `native.explicit-root-without-marker` (native

176	different facts, and neither instrument normalizes the same value differently.
177	Custody-excluded units are explicit unknown required scope, not a successful
178	empty scope; later syntax scanners cannot read their uncustodied source. There is

183	
184	**Pruned trees and the read set (A-5).** "No custody walk" for a pruned tree
185	means discovery neither enumerates units in it nor walks its directories for

193	**Admitted boundary inventory for the language-unit instrument (decided; post-reset

242	## S4. Trust time (AR-04)
243	
244	Definitions. `evalHighWater` (floor F): highest instant at which a decision
245	evaluation was made. `lastAccepted` (L): issue time of the newest accepted
246	signed document; required whenever F exists. **Admitted time evidence** A =
247	max(L, accepted witness time, presented root issue time), where a witness is
248	the newest issue time of a presented payload whose signature already verified
249	and which is not older than L. The wall clock is untrusted.
250	
251	Decision evaluation, in order, for record R, observation (wall W, sleep-
252	inclusive monotonic M, bootId B), optional payload P:
253	
254	1. Payload future check (unchanged FC-FUTURE): an issue time > W + 24 h refuses
255	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`; nothing is written.
256	2. Fresh install (F absent): without admitted time evidence the evaluation
257	   refuses `TRUST.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (the core's embedded bootstrap
258	   payload or an ordinary payload is required); nothing is written. With it,
259	   W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` and initialises nothing.
260	   Otherwise tEval = max(W, A); F := tEval, L := A, anchor := (B, M, W); expiry
261	   states are evaluated from the presented documents, never set to false.
262	3. In-session continuity: if the anchor has the same bootId, expected =
263	   anchorWall + (M − anchorMono). A forward deviation over 24 h refuses
264	   `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` (`in-session`) unless a witness proves the
265	   expectation itself was behind (witness ≥ expected). A backward deviation is
266	   the finding `CLOCK-REGRESSION-IN-SESSION`; a monotonic value below the
267	   anchor's is `CLOCK-CONTINUITY-MALFORMED` (finding, anchor not rewritten).
268	4. Plausibility: W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD`
269	   (`beyond-horizon`) **before any evaluation and before any write**. Remedy:
270	   correct the clock, or present a payload issued within 90 d of W.
271	5. Evaluation: tEval = max(F, W, A). The floor written is exactly tEval
272	   (write-ahead, §5.6 durability), so the persisted floor and the evaluated
273	   instant never differ and no later evaluation runs earlier than an earlier
274	   one. `CLOCK-REGRESSION` (W < F) and `TRUST.FLOOR_AHEAD_OF_WALL`
275	   (F > W + 90 d) are findings with remedies. L advances to A when A > L. The
276	   anchor is rewritten when continuity is unavailable, within tolerance, or
277	   excused by a witness.
278	
279	Consequences. An accidental forward wall is accepted only up to 90 d beyond
280	signed evidence, so a wrong write is bounded and heals as signed time catches
281	up; a larger jump writes nothing. Expiry, staleness and future checks still
282	fail closed at tEval. Repeated reboots cannot lower F or freeze payload
283	freshness: F only rises, and freshness is evaluated at tEval ≥ F. Report-only
284	evaluation (doctor) computes the same decision, states and findings, labels
285	`evaluationMode: report-only`, and returns `writes: []` with every write field
286	null; it cannot create a recovery challenge.
287	
288	### S4.5 Recovery of an already poisoned floor
289	
290	A floor years ahead of real time (written by the superseded rule, or by a
291	restore) cannot be lowered by ordinary payloads: tEval ≥ F keeps every document
292	expired. Recovery is an authenticated, install-bound, single-use act:
293	
294	1. `opensip trust recovery-challenge` (decision mode only; global fence, no
295	   project lease) writes one pending challenge and exports
296	   `trust-recovery-challenge.v1.json` (`TrustRecoveryChallengeV1`): a fresh
297	   32-byte host-CSPRNG nonce, `createdWall`, and `recordDigest` =
298	   metadata-profile digest, domain `opensip.metadata.recovery-challenge.1`,
299	   over the six bound fields `{evalHighWater, lastAccepted, rootVersion,
300	   revocationVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, recoveryEpochSerial}`. The
301	   pending record additionally binds `{bootId, createdMono, expiresMono =
302	   createdMono + 24 h, createdWall}` with sleep-inclusive monotonic time. A
303	   new challenge replaces the pending one; a reboot invalidates it.
304	2. The publisher's recovery service (consented online) or the air-gap ceremony
305	   returns `trust-recovery-epoch.v1.json`: an `opensip-signature-envelope.2`
306	   of kind `trust-recovery-epoch` (digest domain
307	   `opensip.metadata.recovery-epoch.1`) with body `TrustRecoveryEpochV1`
308	   `{recoverySchema:1, kind, epochSerial, issuedAt, challenge{nonce,
309	   recordDigest}, counters{rootVersion, revocationVersion,
310	   indexSnapshotVersion}, installBinding:"challenge"}`. Authority is the
311	   **accepted root's `recoveryAuthority.keys` at `recoveryAuthority.threshold`**
312	   (the existing schema-1 field: 5–16 keys, threshold ≥ 3, disjoint from
313	   `rootKeys`), revoked keys excluded. Root keys never count, so routine
314	   recovery never exercises root keys and root-key compromise alone cannot
315	   lower a floor. The accepted root's expiry is not consulted for this one
316	   document because the floor under repair is what expired it. This is the
317	   only external artifact needed.
318	3. `opensip trust recovery-import` verifies, under the global fence and no
319	   project lease, in this order: (a) **strict closed shape of the epoch and of
320	   the pending record before any comparison** (exact-typed constants: `true`
321	   is never `1`, integers are never booleans, timestamps by grammar, hex by
322	   grammar); (b) recovery-authority threshold; (c) a pending challenge exists,
323	   its `bootId` equals the current boot, and `createdMono ≤ mono ≤
324	   expiresMono` (`CHALLENGE_BOOT_CHANGED`, `CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`,
325	   `CHALLENGE_CONTINUITY_MALFORMED`); (d) nonce equals the pending nonce;
326	   `recordDigest` equals both the pending value and a fresh digest of the
327	   current record; `epochSerial` > `recoveryEpochSerial`; (e) **every counter
328	   equals the challenged record's counter exactly** (`COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`).
329	   A higher signed counter is refused with that typed detail; the remedy is to
330	   import the ordinary payload that carries it and re-challenge. Nothing is
331	   silently discarded and nothing is silently advanced. (f) `issuedAt` ≥ L and
332	   |`issuedAt` − W| ≤ 24 h (`ISSUED_IN_FUTURE`, `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`).
333	   Any failure refuses `RECOVERY.REFUSED` with the typed detail and changes
334	   nothing.
335	4. On success: F := L := `issuedAt`; anchor cleared; `recoveryEpochSerial` :=
336	   `epochSerial`; pending challenge consumed; audit record `RECOVERY-EPOCH`
337	   with the previous floor. Counters, revocation entries, role states,
338	   journals and namespaces are untouched; no namespace is deleted.
339	
340	Threat statement. The wall is untrusted. The single-boot, 24 h monotonic
341	challenge window plus the ±24 h issue skew mean that no response to an old
342	challenge, held indefinitely, can later lower the floor to a stale real time:
343	after a reboot or after the window the response is dead, and inside the window
344	the signed time must sit within a day of the wall the operator is looking at.
345	This bounds a signed epoch relative to the wall; it does not prove the wall.
346	The protocol promises install binding (nonce + record digest), single use,
347	serial monotonicity, exact counter preservation and no floor below L. It makes
348	**no promise against a malicious publisher**: a recovery authority that signs a
349	false time is outside the protocol, exactly as it is for every other signed
350	time in this contract. Why this cannot revive revoked trust: revocation is by
351	counter and entries, which the epoch may not change; a key revoked before the
352	epoch cannot sign it; expiry is re-evaluated at signed real time, which is ≥
353	every earlier signed time, so a document genuinely expired at real time stays
354	expired. If the recovery authority is unavailable, recovery is impossible and
355	the install must be re-established by fresh install or authenticated adoption.
356	Migration and rollback (S9) never carry a pending challenge; the serial moves
357	forward with the other floors.

359	## S5. Root chain through expired roots (AR-05)
360	
361	An install holding accepted root N evaluates a chain N+1..M link by link. Each
362	link needs the previous root's threshold from that root's keys (continuity)
363	**and** the new root's threshold from its own keys (possession), revoked keys
364	excluded from both. Semantic admission per link: reader supports the schema;
365	version and previous-version contiguity; not issued before its predecessor;
366	issue before expiry; root key policy. Intermediate expiry is never consulted;
367	the final root must be unexpired at tEval and not issued more than 24 h after
368	the wall. Any refusal leaves state unchanged and names the link. Success
369	advances the root counter to M and L to the final root's issue time. An expired
370	root with no chain refuses `ROOT.EXPIRED_NO_CHAIN` with the remedy of presenting
371	a payload carrying N+1..newest. Schema-1 readers refuse a schema-2 root as
372	`ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` (typed, not corruption, state unchanged).
373	
374	## S6. Live revocation (AR-05)
375	
376	Trust epoch `{rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion,
377	permissionPolicyDigest}` is captured at operation start. **Authority
378	checkpoint:** every brokered effect request re-reads the epoch under the
379	journal append lock before its intent record. **Observer:** a tick every 5 s
380	reads the counter; if the last successful read is older than 10 s or the read
381	fails, the observer appends `REV(observer-fail-stop)` and cancels. These bounds
382	are implementation qualification obligations under OS scheduling assumptions
383	using `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `mach_continuous_time` (macOS); they are not a
384	wall-clock guarantee inside a stopped process. A stopped process emits no
385	effects; on resume its first checkpoint or tick observes the stall and fail-
386	stops before any further effect.
387	
388	The observation predicate revokes on a higher counter whose entries name the
389	closure (release, signing key, namespace, catalog snapshot) or on a policy
390	digest change that removes a required grant; unrelated changes are recorded as
391	drift; a lower counter never revokes (rollback is detected by the floor rules).
392	
393	**Linearization** is under the single journal append lock: after `REV` no
394	`RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended, and no brokered effect commits.
395	Commit records carry `postimageSha256`. At `REV(trust-revoked)` the host
396	attempts rollback of reversible completed effects **only where the current
397	bytes equal the committed postimage**; a mismatch is `rollbackBlocked`
398	(user-modified since commit, never overwritten), an unreadable target is
399	`indeterminate`. Irreversible completed effects and effects under
400	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every

400	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every
401	residual. Cancellation is bounded: refuse further requests (0 s), protocol
402	Cancel (2 s), SIGTERM (3 s), SIGKILL of the process group and reap (5 s),
403	scratch cleanup under the lease; total 10 s under the same qualification
404	standing. **Unconfined children** (repository code under S10) are not brokered
405	effects: they are cancelled within the bound and disclosed, and their external
406	effects before the kill are not enumerable. No confinement is claimed.

408	## S7. Leases and lock order (AR-14)
409	
410	The current security schema bundle declares every array's `x-opensip-order`
411	under identity §3. Namespace lists use strictly unique raw UTF-8 locator order;
412	execution-grant owner records use strictly unique `ownerKey` order. Public code
413	sets use strictly unique UTF-8 order. Other arrays are explicit sequences unless
414	their owning schema states a stricter order: journal revisions, lock traces,
415	release steps, signature entries and observations are never silently sorted.
416	This collection-admission law does not change the security metadata canonical
417	profile or its immutable historical schemas.
418	
419	| Level | Lock | Carrier | Blocking |
420	|---|---|---|---|
421	| 0 | lifecycle fence | `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`, flock LOCK_EX | bounded wait 5 s, then `PROJECT.BUSY` |
422	| 1 | project writer lease | `<namespace>/writer.lease`, LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB | never |
423	| 2 | project reader lease | `<namespace>/readers.lease`, LOCK_SH\|LOCK_NB (readers); LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB (EXCLUSIVE) | never |
424	| 3 | ledger transaction | SQLite WAL; writers BEGIN IMMEDIATE, busy_timeout 0; readers read a committed snapshot | never for readers |
425	| 4 | journal append lock | in-process mutex | bounded, in-process |
426	
427	Modes: `SHARED-READ` (any number; queries, rendering, doctor, read-only
428	agents), `APPEND-WRITE` (one; analysis, import, baseline pin; publishes only
429	new immutable objects and ledger rows, never deletes or rewrites bytes a reader
430	may reference), `EXCLUSIVE` (GC, purge, migration, repair apply; nothing else
431	held). Readers never block a writer; a second writer or an EXCLUSIVE request
432	gets `PROJECT.BUSY` at once, releases the fence, and may retry outside the
433	fence with backoff 1/2/4/8/15 s within a 30 s budget. Laws: no lease without
434	the fence; no waiting for a lease; no waiting for the fence while holding a
435	lease (operation end releases the lease first); no upgrade; trust state is
436	written only under the fence and never under a lease; GC census is a
437	LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe under the fence and a busy probe means retain.
438	
439	**One-writer refinement (identity-and-evidence §5).** "Exactly one per-project
440	writer holds the lifecycle lease through admission, evaluation and commit" is
441	the APPEND-WRITE mode: exactly one append writer, coexisting with any number of
442	immutable-snapshot readers that never wait on it. The EXCLUSIVE mode is the
443	refinement for migration, purge, GC and repair apply, which need a reader
444	census (the LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe) because they may remove or rewrite bytes a
445	reader could reference. There is no contradiction with the identity contract:
446	readers are invisible to the writer's commit order and the writer is invisible
447	to readers' snapshots. Exact selectors: `<namespace>/writer.lease` LOCK_EX|NB
448	is the identity contract's "lifecycle lease"; `<namespace>/readers.lease`
449	LOCK_SH|NB is its "consistent committed snapshot"; `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`
450	is its "global trust admission and revocation lock order".
451	
452	**Namespaces.** Every project lease names a namespace from the host namespace
453	registry (ProjectId ↔ namespace locator, identity §5); a lease on an
454	unregistered namespace is a violation, never an implicit registration
455	(`lease-on-an-unregistered-namespace-is-refused-negative`). Namespaces are
456	independent: a writer in one never blocks a writer in another.
457	
458	**Core-transition lock set (decided; SHOULD-6).** `core update|repair|rollback`
459	and `store migrate|rollback` change install-level state, while EXCLUSIVE is a
460	per-namespace lease. The mechanism is a composition, not a new flock mode:
461	
462	1. The install-wide fence (level 0) is held for the **whole** transition, not
463	   only for lease acquisition; no project operation can be admitted meanwhile.
464	2. The affected namespace set is enumerated from the registry by
465	   `core_transition_affected_namespaces` (never from user input or a directory
466	   listing): **all registered namespaces** when the from/to state schema differ
467	   or a store is re-selected (`core rollback`, `store migrate|rollback`);
468	   **no namespace** for a same-schema `core update` or `core repair`, because
469	   the selected core closure is an immutable generation, running project
470	   operations keep their pinned generation and re-check trust at their S6
471	   checkpoints, and nothing they reference is rewritten.
472	3. EXCLUSIVE is taken on each affected namespace in namespace-locator byte
473	   order, non-blocking and all-or-nothing: the first busy namespace releases
474	   every acquired lease in reverse order, releases the fence, reports
475	   `PROJECT.BUSY` naming that namespace and its holders, and the retry is the
476	   ordinary backoff outside the fence.
477	4. The `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` (S9.2) names the exact lease set and is
478	   written only after every lease is held: in the lock model the
479	   `transition-journal` action is lawful only under the fence, only after
480	   `core-transition-acquire` succeeded, and only naming exactly the held set
481	   (`transition-journal-*` cases). Crash
482	   recovery runs as the first act under the next fence acquisition, before any
483	   admission, over the S9.2 recovery table (which defers to the S9 footprint
484	   table for store operations), and re-acquires exactly the journaled
485	   set; flock leases die with the process, so no stale lease survives. A
486	   namespace registered after the intent cannot exist (registration needs the
487	   fence); finding one is `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`.
488	5. Leases are released in reverse order, then the fence. The fence cannot be
489	   released while transition leases are held.
490	
491	Ordinary component `install`/`update` publish new immutable generations under
492	the fence alone and never revoke a generation a live operation pins (removal
493	is GC census only). GC iterates registered namespaces and treats a busy
494	namespace as retain, never as refusal. Reference `lease_schedule` (registry,
495	`core-transition-acquire|release`, `transition-journal`),
496	`core_transition_affected_namespaces`; cases `core-transition-*`,
497	`transition-journal-*`, `two-namespaces-are-independent-*`.
498	
499	Command → lease map (workflows command inventory):
500	
501	| Lease | Commands |
502	|---|---|
503	| none (fence only, no project lock) | `install`, `update` (component generations), `trust refresh|import|recovery-challenge|recovery-import`, ordinary payload import, `doctor` / `trust doctor` / `store status` (report-only, no write) |
504	| SHARED-READ | `query`, `recommend`, `baseline show`, `policy show|test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview`, `agent serve` reads, `doctor` project checks |
505	| APPEND-WRITE | `opensip` default, `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `test run`, `native prepare`, `repair verify` |
506	| EXCLUSIVE (one namespace) | `repair apply` (S10.1 authorization), `repair recover --apply-recovery` (S10.2 authorization; inspection alone is SHARED-READ), `purge`, `store gc` per namespace (busy = retain) |
507	| core-transition lock set (fence held + EXCLUSIVE on every affected registered namespace) | `core update`, `core repair`, `core rollback`, `store migrate`, `store rollback` |
508	
509	Trust recovery deliberately takes no project lease: it mutates SC-TRUST only,
510	under the fence, and a project operation that starts afterwards observes the
511	new floor at its trust instant.

565	
566	Bridge. Stage 1: root readers {1}, state decoder v1, TR-REPAIR typed absence,
567	`kernelAttestationKeys` empty. Stage 2: root readers {1, 2}, state decoders
568	`state-decoder.v1` (read-only migration source) and `state-decoder.v2`
569	(writer); schema-2 roots may carry an active TR-REPAIR (threshold ≥ 2, keys ≥
570	threshold + 1, namespaces present, no reuse of root keys) and up to 8 kernel
571	attestation keys (no reuse of root keys). Ordered release: (1) the stage-2 core
572	ships under the schema-1 catalog, so every stage-1 install updates by its
573	ordinary path; (2) root N+1 with schema 2 is signed by root-N keys and its own
574	keys; (3) stage-1 cores refuse N+1 typed and keep N until it expires; stage-2
575	cores accept it by the dual reader; (4) state migration 1→2 runs under
576	EXCLUSIVE. Both stages keep the metadata profile of S2.

578	Migration writes a `migrating` root: PREPARING → PREPARED → (old store fenced
579	`RESTORED`) → COMMITTED → final rename. Recovery from the durable footprint
580	only: absent = nothing to do; PREPARING or PREPARED with the old store unfenced
581	= abort; PREPARED with the old store fenced = resume from step 3; COMMITTED =
582	resume the final rename; final and migrating coexisting, or unknown state =
583	quarantine `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. Floors (`rootVersion`, `indexSnapshotVersion`,

588	`ROOT.FLOOR_ABOVE_CORE`. Rollback inside the 30 d window re-selects the retained
589	old store with floors set to the maximum of both stores; it refuses when the
590	new store accepted a root the old core cannot verify (schema or chain reach). A
591	poisoned floor is not lowered by migration or rollback; only S4.5 lowers it.

712	fence, before any project admission.** Fail closed: no fence → refuse; a

722	the rollback window); `DONE`/`ABORTED` → release only. Cases `crash-at-*`,

854	### S10.2 Repair recovery authorization (decided; post-reset v2 N-4/P9)
855	
856	Recovery inspection (`repair recover` without `--apply-recovery`, workflows §6
857	`repair_inspect`) is read-only and needs no authorization. Every recovery
858	**mutation** (`discard-temps`, `roll-back-renamed`,
859	`verify-postimages-and-commit`) is a separately authorized host-brokered
860	write within the **original** plan's authority, under the EXCLUSIVE lease, and
861	its authorization is the closed security record `RepairRecoveryAuthorizationV1`
862	(product data; identity `H("security.repair-recovery-authorization.v1", record)`
863	is the workflow `RepairApplyJournalV1.recoveryAuthorizationRef`, always the full
864	reference, never a truncated prefix). It is admitted by
865	`admit_recovery_authorization(authz, ctx)` only when every binding holds:
866	
867	- **Project, plan, snapshot, recipe.** `projectId`, `repairPlanId`,
868	  `baseSnapshotId` and `recipeClosureId` equal the admitted project and the
869	  rehashed original plan (`AUTHZ.*_MISMATCH`).
870	- **Exact journal identity (noncircular).** `journalRef` =
871	  `security.repair-apply-journal-identity.v1:` + `H` over the closed identity
872	  preimage `{schemaFamily, schemaMajor, requestId, stepId, executionId,
873	  repairPlanId, baseSnapshotId, authorizationRef}`: only fields fixed when the
874	  apply journal was created, never `state`, paths, blobs, blocked/restore lists
875	  or any `recoveryAuthorizationRef` the journal later carries, so one journal
876	  has one identity in every state and the reference written into the journal
877	  never enters its own preimage (`journal-identity-mismatch-*`,
878	  `journal-of-a-different-plan-*`).
879	- **Observed journal state and replay/crash semantics.** `journalState` and
880	  `observedJournalStateDigest` (raw SHA-256 of canonical `{state, stagedPaths,
881	  appliedPaths, preimageBlobs}`) equal the journal **as read under the EXCLUSIVE
882	  lease before any recovery write**. Every successful recovery mutation changes
883	  `state`, so a retained authorization cannot be replayed after one
884	  (`AUTHZ.JOURNAL_STATE_MOVED`; `replay-after-a-successful-rollback-*`); a crash
885	  or a `requires-broker` return before the first write leaves the digest
886	  unchanged. The same authorization may continue only within the same still-admitted
887	  recovery execution and lifetime. A process crash ends that execution; a fresh
888	  attempt requires a newly admitted authorization bound to its new execution id (`crash-before-the-first-recovery-write-*`).
889	- **Finite action.** `recoveryAction` equals the one the journal state admits
890	  (`PREPARING`/`STAGED` → `discard-temps`; `APPLYING` → `roll-back-renamed`;
891	  `APPLIED`/`INDETERMINATE` → `verify-postimages-and-commit`;
892	  `AUTHZ.RECOVERY_ACTION_MISMATCH` otherwise). Terminal states (`COMMITTED`,
893	  `FAILED_*`, `RECOVERY_BLOCKED`) admit no mutation
894	  (`AUTHZ.RECOVERY_NOT_MUTATING:<state>`); the table mirrors the workflow
895	  recovery table's mutating rows, and the integration checker asserts that equality today
896	  (`security-workflow-recovery-action-table-identical`, comparing the mutating rows of
897	  `W.RECOVERY_TABLE` with `S.RECOVERY_ACTION_FOR_STATE`).
898	- **Fresh attempt.** `originalRequestId` equals the journal's `requestId`;
899	  `recoveryRequestId`/`recoveryExecutionId` equal the recovery invocation's own
900	  ids and differ from the original (`AUTHZ.RECOVERY_REQUEST_NOT_FRESH`).
901	- **Consent and policy.** Consent is `interactive-explicit` (never in CI) or
902	  `policy-record`, with a real boolean `ci` equal to the invocation's; the project
903	  policy admits repair.
904	- **Time.** `issuedAt` ≤ S4 admitted evaluation time ≤ `expiresAt`, lifetime at
905	  most 24 h; no admitted time context refuses (`AUTHZ.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT`).
906	- **Boundary.** `leaseMode` `EXCLUSIVE`, `mutationBoundary` `host-broker`,
907	  `repositoryExecution` and `newEdits` are the constant `false`: recovery can
908	  never grant repository code execution, write a byte the original plan did not
909	  name, or broaden the plan (`planScope: original-plan-only`).
910	- **Current host custody.** The S3 custody rule is re-run on the recovery
911	  invocation (`AUTHZ.CUSTODY_NOT_ADMITTED`); an old admission does not carry over.
912	
913	**Safe rollback versus re-executing a revoked recipe.** `discard-temps` and
914	`roll-back-renamed` restore retained preimages or discard temps and **never
915	consult recipe trust**: rolling back after the recipe was revoked is exactly what
916	revocation rollback is (`rollback-recovery-admits-although-the-recipe-closure-is-revoked-*`).
917	`verify-postimages-and-commit` would commit the recipe's postimages, so it
918	re-consults current signed-closure trust: a revoked recipe refuses first
919	(`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, D9 `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`) and a recipe
920	not positively admitted refuses (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_NOT_ADMITTED`). The
921	workflow recovery table's guarded preimage/postimage law (every target at its
922	plan preimage or postimage before any restore or commit; otherwise
923	`RECOVERY_BLOCKED`) is mandatory and never waived by this record.
924	
925	**Trusted context inputs**, each a host observation and none supplied by the
926	caller of `repair recover`: `projectId`, `repairPlanId`, `baseSnapshotId`,
927	`journal` (as read under the lease), `recoveryRequestId`, `recoveryExecutionId`,

929	`revokedClosures`, `admittedClosures`. Output `RecoveryAuthorizationAdmissionV1`;

971	### S12.1 Projecting a refusal onto the one closed public detail vocabulary
972	
973	A public termination carries exactly one `domainDetail` = `{code, remedy, subject?}`, and `code` is a
974	member of the single closed registry (`design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json`, mirrored by
975	`workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/DomainDetailCode`). This section states the projection
976	this unit's refusals take, so that "detail" in the prose above is never ambiguous between a registry
977	member and free subject text. Reference `public_detail` / `public_details`, record
978	`PublicDetailProjectionV1`, fixture `public-detail-cases.v1.json`, sweep
979	`public-domain-details-are-a-closed-set-with-a-bounded-pending-registration-gap`.
980	
981	1. **Base code, then subject.** The base code is everything before the **first** colon; everything
982	   after it is subject data. `ROOT.ROLE_SET:1` is code `ROOT.ROLE_SET`, subject `1`.
983	2. **A registered detail wins over the enclosing refusal.** When a refusal carries a `detail` whose
984	   base code is a registry member, that is the public code. This is why the 38 `ROOT.*` document
985	   defects are public codes instead of collapsing into one `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`, and it is
986	   exactly why `ENVELOPE.*` and `PROFILE_SET.*` belong in the registry: they occupy the same position
987	   in `admit_profile_set_envelope` that `ROOT.*` occupies in `admit_root_document`, and S9.1 names
988	   them normatively as `detail`.
989	3. **Otherwise the refusal supplies the code and the whole detail is subject text.** This is the
990	   existing reading for `RECOVERY.REFUSED` (`CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`, `COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`,
991	   `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`, …), for `CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED` (`SYMLINK`, `WRITABLE_BY_OTHERS`, …)
992	   and for `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`, `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE`, …). Those
993	   sub-details are deliberately **not** registry members; registering them would create a second
994	   public vocabulary for the same events.
995	4. **The vocabulary is closed, not a prefix rule.** The unit declares the exact set it may emit
996	   (`SECURITY_PUBLIC_DETAIL_CODES`, 191 members). A detail whose base code lies inside one of the
997	   eight families this unit publishes (`AUTHZ.`, `ENVELOPE.`, `GRANT.`, `NT-TCB-`, `PLAN.`,
998	   `PROFILE_SET.`, `ROOT.`, `TRANSITION.`) but outside that set **refuses**; there is no open
999	   `PROFILE_SET.*` wildcard.
1000	5. **The D9 branch comes from the refusal, never from the detail.** Naming a defect more precisely
1001	   never changes its termination branch. `PROFILE_SET.NO_TR_PROFILE_ROLE` therefore travels under
1002	   `ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` → `REQUEST.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED` exactly as S9.1 says, while every
1003	   other `PROFILE_SET.*`/`ENVELOPE.*` defect travels under `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE` →
1004	   `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`. Members of the three document-admission families
1005	   (`ROOT.`, `ENVELOPE.`, `PROFILE_SET.`) that the D9 table does not name individually take that same
1006	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE` row; the three schema-major refusals keep their own. The single
1007	   exception is `AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, which is an admission rejection while every other
1008	   `AUTHZ.*` detail of the same admission is a precondition failure.

1158	The baseline is the separate `opensip-cli` prototype at commit `a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0`, as scoped by architecture `prototype-evidence-reference.md`. S9's signed product stage/schema bridge must never be applied to a prototype database merely because it contains a version number of one.
1159	
1160	The complete transition policy is **immutable coexistence with explicit adoption**, not automatic state conversion. Installing or selecting the new product does not replace the prototype package, mutate its Node/npm installation, take over its launcher/PATH alias, import its database, adopt its baselines or run it. Both installations may remain usable through their explicitly selected launchers/absolute paths. New product state is admitted only under its own validated root/profile/namespace; an occupied root with a foreign/prototype marker/schema is refused by the existing root/schema admission before a write. A user chooses a distinct admitted location or project checkout; the host never guesses that overwriting foreign state is migration. Removal targets the selected product installation and its own references. It does not uninstall the prototype or purge either product's evidence by implication.
1161	
1162	A legacy configuration is accepted only by admission §1.1's exact supported legacy schema and in-memory provenance-preserving projection. If the prototype and new product need incompatible project configurations, coexistence uses separate explicitly selected checkouts/configurations rather than silently changing the prototype's tracked intent. Historical exports remain inspectable by their original tools; a separately admitted current-format observation may enter only through the ordinary closed import registry with truthful producer/source correspondence. It cannot acquire historical Run authority or become a baseline merely by changing an id or schema label. This is a settled compatibility boundary for the full product, not a deferred delivery-stage decision.

1	# Evidence workflows and product contracts
2	
3	**Standing:** Acceptance, exact reviewed bytes, and reversibility are recorded
4	in [D-370](../../coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md#d-370--fallow-informed-product-design).
5	**Scope:** Design constraints settled before implementation; the D-369 preview
6	remains the selected implementation scope. This chapter adds no executable
7	capability, public command, wire field, identity recipe, or release qualification.
8	
9	The [Fallow borrow register](../../coop/FALLOW-BORROW-REGISTER.md) maps the
10	original seven ideas and eight further observations to their sources and these
11	decisions. Fallow is design evidence, not a dependency or an authority over
12	OpenSIP semantics.
13	
14	## 1. Scope and ownership
15	
16	OpenSIP's product remains an evidence compiler with one host. Providers supply
17	declared facts and Coverage; rules declare predicates and evidence requirements;
18	the pure evaluator computes policy results; the host owns admission, identity,
19	configuration, supervision, and projections. Model-assisted exploration and
20	external review remain advisory under the [Map/Control boundary](../../MAP-VS-CONTROL.md).
21	No model call or external judgment becomes a required input to Control.
22	
23	These commitments refine that architecture in two ways:
24	
25	- **Preview implementation guidance** explains existing obligations: explicit
26	  insufficiency, consistent human/JSON meaning, deterministic declared inputs,
27	  host-owned common behavior, and refusal of unsupported operations. It changes
28	  no preview schema, threshold, supported platform, required gate, or row grade.
29	- **Future capability constraints** settle ownership, evidence handoffs, and
30	  failure semantics now. Before a future capability enters a supported slice,
31	  its owning register rows must accept the concrete schemas, identity and
32	  lifecycle joins, fixtures, resource limits, and product scope it needs.
33	
34	The [reference handoff](../../coop/completion/reference-architecture.v2.md)
35	continues to own the exact preview: `analyze`, `doctor`, help/version, one
36	TypeScript provider, and the bundled import-cycle rule. This chapter does not
37	enable a baseline, repair, review, discovery command, additional rule pack,
38	runtime importer, semantic-similarity model, durable result cache, or Map.
39	Existing admission must continue to refuse excluded forms. A future feature is
40	not implemented by reserving an undocumented flag or accepting an open payload.
41	
42	## 2. Discovery and zero-config behavior
43	
44	For each supported conventional project shape, the product goal is useful
45	analysis without requiring a user-authored OpenSIP configuration. An installed,
46	compatible analysis closure is a prerequisite; zero-config is not permission to
47	download tools, execute repository configuration, or grant effects implicitly.
48	
49	Discovery distinguishes three kinds of information:
50	
51	| Information | Owner and treatment |
52	|---|---|
53	| Observed technical facts: language, manifest, workspace layout, recognized convention | Discovery producer reports the source and uncertainty; the host validates and resolves applicability. |
54	| Product defaults: supported ignore conventions and default profile selection | Host-owned, versioned, disclosed, and overridable through existing configuration precedence. |
55	| Project decisions: gate strictness, allowed dependencies, waivers, boundary intent | Explicit project policy; a detector or recommender cannot adopt these on the project's behalf. |
56	
57	Any discovered value that affects analysis must enter the ordinary declared
58	input/resolution path with provenance. There is no seventh configuration layer,
59	provider-private override, or hidden environment input. An explicit supported
60	override wins according to the existing resolver; ambiguity is disclosed rather
61	than silently selecting a broader or weaker interpretation. Ignored and
62	unsupported regions are scope information, never evidence that those regions
63	are clean.
64	
65	A future recommendation surface returns detected evidence, proposed settings,
66	default rationale, unresolved choices, and the effect of each choice. Reading a
67	recommendation does not write configuration. Applying it is a separate host
68	operation with the normal write authority. Proposed settings must be accepted
69	by the actual strict configuration resolver, not merely validate against a
70	JSON Schema; schema references must resolve from the supported offline closure.
71	The preview's read-only `doctor`
72	does not become a source analyzer or execute configuration to make detection
73	more convenient.
74	
75	Qualification for newly supported project conventions should use pinned real
76	repository shapes and nearby negative cases, including generated sources,
77	monorepo consumers, and convention-loaded entry points. Record how many manual
78	corrections are needed for a useful result and which gaps remain. Repeated
79	workarounds are investigation inputs, not automatically confirmed bugs or
80	permission to collect private repositories. Exact corpus and numeric targets
81	belong to the capability's later qualification decision; no target is invented
82	here.
83	
84	## 3. Evidence sufficiency and visible omissions
85	
86	Preserve C-1: evidence is sufficient for a particular predicate over a declared
87	scope. Syntax, resolved symbols, tests, runtime observations, and repository
88	history do not form one global strength or confidence ranking. Independent
89	evidence may support different claims about the same subject without being
90	collapsed into a single score.
91	
92	Every supported assessment projection must preserve the distinction between:
93	
94	- completed analysis with no matches in the admitted scope;
95	- unsupported, disabled, or inapplicable analysis; and
96	- attempted analysis with missing, failed, truncated, or insufficient evidence.
97	
98	These are semantic distinctions, not new wire-enum spellings. Existing typed
99	Coverage and diagnostics carry preview meaning. Future schemas must retain the
100	selected scope, applicable requirements, omissions and reasons, and truncation
101	or completion information needed to interpret the result. A count is meaningful
102	only together with that scope and sufficiency. Cancelling or exhausting a
103	budget cannot produce a clean result from a truncated subject set.
104	
105	Optional evidence can be absent while independently sufficient predicates still
106	complete. A predicate whose required evidence is missing remains indeterminate;
107	reporting other completed predicates cannot make it pass. A syntactic fact may
108	satisfy a syntactic predicate, but cannot substitute for required semantic
109	resolution. A summary or renderer must not erase this distinction.
110	
111	## 4. Candidate, inspection, and review handoffs
112	
113	Future advisory discovery separates observations from judgments. A candidate
114	means that investigation is warranted; it is neither a proven finding nor a
115	policy outcome. Deterministic clone detection describes exact or normalized
116	structure under a named algorithm. Model-based similarity remains a separate
117	Map capability: a score is model-specific and does not prove behavioral
118	equivalence or refactor safety. This separation replaces the proposed single
119	progression from exact clones to supposedly stronger semantic confidence.
120	
121	An inspection request selects an exact candidate from an explicit discovery
122	result. Its handoff binds the project, source subjects with their content
123	identity (the sealed Snapshot or per-subject content digests), scope,
124	producer/schema versions, relevant parameters, and completion information. Inspection either
125	uses retained source evidence or validates the currently opened source against
126	that handoff. Stale, missing, ambiguous, or outside-scope subjects are reported
127	explicitly. It cannot silently rerun retrieval and substitute a new candidate.
128	
129	External reviews remain separate artifacts referencing the reviewed result and
130	subject binding. A later review-join operation validates supported versions,
131	membership, duplicate judgments, and source correspondence. Unreviewed
132	candidates remain visible; requiring every candidate to be reviewed is an
133	explicit workflow condition. Matching an identifier validates correlation, not
134	the truth of an agent's prose. Missing or contradictory evidence permits
135	abstention.
136	
137	An advisory item claiming to cite Control must reference an actual host-emitted
138	item in its named view; unknown references are rejected. Map may also produce
139	its own labeled observations or hypotheses under its separate contract. Those
140	do not become Control citations merely because they mention the same file.
141	
142	Keep three questions independent: whether the candidate merits investigation,
143	whether the compared behavior is equivalent, and whether a proposed refactor is
144	safe in context. A favorable similarity score answers none of them by itself.
145	No external verdict edits the original observations or directly changes a
146	Control result, waiver, baseline, or exit. Any supported future human policy
147	action must use its own host-owned policy path.
148	
149	These are required binding dimensions, not new durable identifier recipes.
150	Candidate and review identities, retained source policy, and review storage must
151	be designed under the owning future contracts. Preview correlation identifiers
152	must not be advertised as stable finding identities or sealed Runs.
153	
154	## 5. Remediation requires its own evidence
155	
156	A future repair recipe declares the action, exact target binding, evidence
157	requirements, permitted edit scope, and verification obligations. Reporting a
158	candidate does not make its removal safe. "No references in the checked scope"
159	is distinct from "no possible consumers"; unresolved owning projects, dynamic
160	dispatch, external consumers, or incomplete runtime observation remain explicit
161	limitations relevant to the particular repair.
162	
163	The repair lifecycle has separate preview and apply operations. A preview
164	describes edits and unmet preconditions without changing source. Apply checks
165	current source identity, current authorization, and evidence sufficiency at the
166	mutation boundary. A source change or evidence mismatch invalidates the plan;
167	the host refuses it and requires a new preview instead of relocating an edit
168	heuristically. A component cannot mutate source independently of the host.
169	
170	Verification runs against the resulting source through ordinary analysis and
171	any declared, separately authorized tests. An applied edit and a verified
172	outcome are distinct results. Failed verification cannot be presented as a
173	successful repair. Multi-file atomicity, interruption, partial edits, rollback
174	ownership, and exact verification outcomes must be closed in the repair
175	contract before apply is supported. This chapter does not select a filesystem
176	transaction algorithm or authorize a test runner in the preview.
177	
178	## 6. Delta attribution and policy changes
179	
180	Preserve the existing versioned fingerprint and detector-pivot architecture.
181	A finding difference alone cannot establish a code regression when the
182	detector, rule selection, parameters, scope, required evidence, or policy also
183	changed. Baseline adoption remains an explicit host-owned policy operation.
184	
185	A future comparison identifies both source snapshots and both analysis/policy
186	contexts. It separates code-introduced or code-fixed results from detector
187	changes, policy changes, scope changes, waivers, and changes in evidence
188	availability. Use controlled comparisons under compatible semantics to make an
189	attribution; otherwise report the affected comparison as indeterminate. Do not
190	rename an unclassifiable result "inherited" or count a vanished finding as fixed
191	merely because its rule was disabled or its file ignored.
192	
193	The report/gate scope is distinct from the fact derivation scope. A PR may gate
194	only introduced findings while analysis still requires unchanged consumers,
195	entry points, dependencies, or test relationships. Restricting output to changed
196	lines does not establish a complete graph over just those lines. Supplied diff
197	scope and comparison base must agree or be reported incompatible; clone-group
198	reshaping alone does not prove new duplicated code was written.
199	
200	Policy deltas should use schema-aware semantics: raising a maximum allowed
201	complexity weakens it, while lowering a minimum coverage weakens that policy.
202	String matching or the direction of a number alone is not an enforcement rule.
203	The host projects tracked policy changes; new/removed/skipped tests and removed
204	CI steps may also be advisory review observations with stated detection limits.
205	
206	Metrics are reported with their population and unit. A smaller worst function,
207	more functions, and unchanged branching may describe decomposition, which can
208	improve readability without removing decisions. Do not claim behavioral
209	simplification from that metric alone. A suppression changes handling of a
210	finding, not the measured source property. Future waiver/suppression inventory
211	should expose rationale, scope, and staleness using the owning policy contract.
212	
213	## 7. Runtime, test, and history evidence
214	
215	Future evidence import is explicit, bounded, and local-first. Collection or
216	network retrieval is a separate capability and authority decision; analyzing a
217	repository does not implicitly execute tests or start production monitoring.
218	
219	Runtime evidence must state source/build correspondence, capture provenance,
220	observation window, observed population, mapping gaps, and which subjects were
221	observable. Distinguish observed execution, observable-but-unhit code, and code
222	the capture could not observe. An unmatched build or missing source map cannot
223	be treated as an unhit function. A test coverage artifact does not establish
224	production traffic, and an absence of hits during one window does not prove
225	code is safe to delete.
226	
227	Tests and history similarly retain source correspondence, collection scope,
228	tool/version provenance where relevant, and limitations. An impact-selected
229	test list is a bounded recommendation unless the evidence establishes the
230	claimed selection completeness. History or runtime importance may guide
231	advisory review priority; any future deterministic policy over these inputs
232	requires a separately admitted artifact and a declared predicate. Evidence
233	conflicts and gaps remain visible rather than being averaged into confidence.
234	
235	Runtime execution coverage is distinct from OpenSIP Coverage, which describes
236	analysis sufficiency. Freshness, retention, artifact admission, data privacy,
237	and exact source-map/build binding require concrete future contracts. The
238	preview's SC-CACHE/SC-OPS/SC-TRUST state selection is unchanged; no runtime or
239	review evidence store is smuggled into an operational cache.
240	
241	## 8. Common contracts and evidence reuse
242	
243	Implement common behavior from one host-owned declaration registry or generated
244	contract source, with drift checks against the actual supported operations and
245	schemas. Public inventories should describe rules/capabilities, accepted input
246	and output schemas, applicability, supported projections, stable diagnostic
247	codes, and action availability from their owning contracts. The exact signed
248	component schema remains its existing owner; this registry neither adds an
249	unsigned capability claim nor creates a plugin ABI.
250	
251	Rule/contribution updates cannot silently select project policy, introduce a
252	private configuration precedence, or change gate behavior through recommended
253	defaults. Host admission validates declarations even if a component uses the
254	SDK. Independent release compatibility remains per surface; generated artifacts
255	must not force all components onto one release version.
256	
257	Generate or drift-check factual help/schema/adapter inventories from the same
258	source. Keep audience-specific explanation separate, but flag it for review when
259	its underlying contract changes. Tests must cover supported human/JSON
260	semantics in the preview and each additional adapter when advertised; a core
261	test alone does not demonstrate that an adapter preserves the result.
262	
263	Report formatting consumes an explicit typed assessment; it does not crawl the
264	working tree, run an analyzer, read physical tables, or recompute findings.
265	Expensive facts can be shared within a valid analysis operation. Future saved
266	reports and inspection surfaces use the common typed query boundary and disclose
267	unavailable retained evidence instead of reconstructing it invisibly. Source
268	enrichment is an explicit inspection operation, not a renderer side effect.
269	Cross-run result reuse remains excluded from the preview. Exact acceleration
270	and semantic production retain the distinction in the Gortex borrow register.
271	
272	## 9. Coherent workflows and bounded review
273	
274	Preserve one host invocation containing typed steps. A named workflow is data
275	selecting existing host-owned operations, not a peer tool with private policy,
276	persistence, command hooks, or exits. Step requirements and dependencies must be
277	explicit; aggregation cannot hide a failed or indeterminate required step.
278	The existing Plan/workflow contracts own exact identity, cancellation, outcome,
279	and future parent/child links. No extra Invocation or Run identity is defined
280	here, and the preview is still the single supported analysis path.
281	
282	A future review brief and target inspection compose existing evidence. The
283	brief may prioritize boundary crossings, public contract changes, dependency
284	changes, consumers outside the diff, and test/runtime/history context when
285	available. Deterministic selection records its version, inputs, reasons, scope,
286	limits, and omissions. A bounded top list is a view over findings, never a
287	policy truncation: omitted findings still participate in their ordinary gate.
288	Any agent framing remains separately identified and advisory. User research and
289	measurements should choose the list size; Fallow's three-to-five limit is not
290	adopted as an OpenSIP constant.
291	
292	## 10. Declarative policy authoring
293	
294	Future policy authoring should supply schema guidance, rule explanations,
295	positive and negative examples, and an explicit preview/test operation before
296	enforcement. Preview reports the effective policy and proposed change; it does
297	not rewrite tracked intent or promote a rule's severity implicitly. Test
298	overrides must be disclosed and scoped to that invocation.
299	
300	Packs remain data-only contributions evaluated under host authority. A rule
301	such as "this layer does not perform network access" must distinguish a ban on
302	known direct calls from a transitive absence-of-effects claim. The latter needs
303	appropriate semantic relations and complete scope; an unknown callee is not
304	evidence of purity. No effect catalogue from another analyzer is accepted as
305	universal effect semantics.
306	
307	The preview accepts only its bundled cycle pack. External packs, additional
308	rules, pack-test commands, and admission of user-authored policies retain their
309	existing scope re-entry requirements.
310	
311	## 11. Integration and future acceptance
312	
313	The architectural decisions in sections 2–10 are settled here; exact public
314	schemas and algorithms for excluded capabilities are not represented as
315	implementation-ready. Their scope admission must satisfy these constraints and
316	the owning rows in the [central readiness register](08-decision-and-readiness-register.md):
317	
318	| Design area | Existing ownership to revisit when scope enters |
319	|---|---|
320	| Discovery, defaults, common declaration registry | DR-103, DR-117, DR-120, DR-123, DR-125; language applicability DR-118 |
321	| Sufficiency, native facts, richer evidence | DR-004, DR-005, DR-118, DR-133; runtime effects/security DR-105/117 |
322	| Candidates, review, runtime retention, repair | DR-002, DR-006–009, DR-105, DR-117; Map boundary and state ownership DR-109/124 |
323	| Baseline and policy attribution | DR-002, DR-006–008, DR-011, DR-111; policy provenance DR-103 |
324	| Workflow, projections, rule-authoring surfaces | DR-117, DR-122/123/125, DR-131; future pack admission under the product boundary |
325	
326	This is an ownership map, not another readiness checklist. No row is closed or
327	regraded here. File 08 and its D-369 after-image remain unchanged because the
328	preview's accepted behavior and gates are unchanged. The decision register and
329	current reading path link this supplement now, before implementation begins.
330	
331	Future qualification must exercise the actual capability input path, including
332	unknown/partial evidence, source changes between review and apply, invalid
333	review membership, policy-only changes, incompatible comparisons, and bounded
334	output. Those are acceptance obligations for the future capability, not claims
335	that newly authored product fixtures or passing runtime tests exist today.
336

"foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json"

"raw SHA-256 of the exact full bytes of that file"

"C (identity-and-evidence section 3 canonical JSON)"
== ladderAuthority
"This registry is the SINGLE authority for every relation's resolution ladder, as identity-and-evidence section 3 states. `ladder` is that relation's total order over its OWN resolution methods, listed weakest-first, inherited verbatim from fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry.relations[].ladder (plus [observed] for unresolved-edge). Every other copy in the kit - native_evidence_model.v2.py LADDERS and capability-manifest-domains.v2.json RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.ladders - is a declared MIRROR of this array and is drift-checked against it exactly and IN ORDER. A one-rung ladder is not a deficiency; it means the relation is fully determined at that rung."
== rungsAreFieldRulesNotTheLadder
"`rungs` is a different table: the per-rung required/forbidden PAYLOAD FIELD rules. It is legitimately the empty object for a relation with no per-rung field variance, which is every single-rung relation. Reading `rungs` as the ladder is the defect this key exists to prevent: an empty field-rule table must never be read as an absent ladder, and never as a licence to skip ladder membership. Membership is checked against `ladder`, always, with no fallback."
== membershipRule
"A resolution is admissible for a relation only if it is a member of THAT relation's `ladder`. A rung that is a member of another relation's ladder is refused, not accepted as a live vocabulary token; the flat rung vocabulary published elsewhere is necessary but never sufficient. Order comparison is the index within one relation's ladder; nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another, and there is no global rank."
== subjectKindLaw
"What a subject-scope's `subjects` entries IDENTIFY, per relation. `source-path`: each subject is a path in the snapshot this scope names, so the scope's own extent is exactly those paths - `file` and `vcs-change` bind it through their registry snapshotJoins pathField, and `clones` binds it through bodyIdentityJoin, whose single anchor IS the body span the identity is over. `package-name`: a package identifier, not a path. `symbol`: an opaque SubjectIdV1 that the record associates with no path; the enumerator's attribution of symbols to files is trusted and is NOT re-derivable from the retained Run, so no per-subject path law is possible for these relations and any capability question about them can only be answered at the coarser retained extent. That limit is stated rather than worked around: inventing symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence."
== anchorLaw
{
 "standing": "Normative and CLOSED. Every relation row carries an `anchorLaw`; there is no default and no unstated relation. It decides how many `fact.anchors` entries a fact of that relation carries, and therefore whether one semantic input has one spelling or several.",
 "whyThisIsARegistryLaw": "`fact.anchors` is `minItems`-free in the identity schema and only `clones` ever stated a cardinality. Every predicate written over the array - the `file` row's `anchorPathField`, and native-evidence section 1.2's `every one of its anchor paths` - is universally quantified, so at ZERO anchors it is vacuously TRUE and neither permits nor forbids that spelling. On the frozen v13 reference BOTH the whole-file-anchored and the unanchored spelling of one `file@enumerated` claim close a Run, with DIFFERENT fact2 identities (`5cce76d9...` and `d7bb2235...` over `tool/main.py`). Nothing here promises cross-prov
== coverageTotalityLaw
{
 "standing": "Normative and CLOSED. A relation row carries a `coverageTotality` row only where the relation's own meaning makes its rung TOTAL over the snapshot inventory. A relation with no row declares that a subject may lawfully bear no fact, which is itself the record that nothing further constrains it.",

On frozen v13 that graph closed - a `file@enumerated` scope over the inventoried subject `a.ts`, `coverage: complete`, `deficiency: null` and zero facts. Nothing derived the obligation, so nothing refused it.",
 "whichRelationsHaveOne": "`file@enumerated` only. }

The OMISSION half is coverageTotalityLaw above and is owed only where a relation carries a coverageTotality row. These two halves have different owners and different decidability, and neither implies the other.",

It is NOT asserted that every consumer necessarily double-counts; what is established, and what this law fixes, is that the published partition property was not decided anywhere. "Normative. Each row states what the enclosing fact snapshot must contain for this relation payload to be admissible.                            else text)

                protocol_major=3):

        desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "kind": kind,
                "manifestDigest": self.w.raw(manifest),
                "tree": rows, "semanticVersion": semver,
                "protocolMajor": protocol_major, "platform": platform}
        cid, _ = self.w.mint("closure", desc)

    def mint_native(self, domain, descriptor):

    def snapshot(self, config, scope, vcs_kind="git", commit="c" * 40,

               "commitId": commit if vcs_kind != "none" else None,
               "dirty": dirty, "sourceInventoryDigest": raw_digest(inv)}
        desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "projectId": self.w.projectId,
                "sourceInventory": inv,
                "resolvedConfigDigest": self.w.record(config),
                "scopeDigest": self.w.record(scope),
                "vcsDigest": self.w.record(vcs)}
        sid, _ = self.w.mint("snapshot", desc)
        return sid, desc

    def scope(self, snapshot_id, source_u, target_u, relation, rung,
              enumerator, subjects):
        desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "snapshotId": snapshot_id,
                "sourceUniverse": source_u, "targetUniverse": target_u,
                "relation": relation, "resolution": rung,
                "enumeratorClosure": enumerator,
                "subjects": sorted(set(subjects), key=lambda s: C(s))}
        sid, hx = self.w.mint("subject-scope", desc)
        return sid, hx, desc

             payload, anchors, confidence=1000000):

                "relation": relation, "resolution": rung,
                "sourceUniverse": source_u, "targetUniverse": target_u,
                "producerClosure": producer,

                "payloadDigest": self.w.record(payload),
                "anchors": sorted(anchors, key=lambda a: C(a)),

        fid, _ = self.w.mint("fact", desc)
        return fid, desc

        entry.setdefault("resolution", scope_desc["resolution"])

                "payloadSchemaDigest": G.NATIVE_DOC_DIGEST,

        return cid, desc, payload

             schema_digests):

                "scopeIds": sorted(set(scope_ids), key=lambda s: C(s)),
                "facts": sorted(set(fact_ids), key=lambda s: C(s)),
                "coverageIds": sorted(set(coverage_ids), key=lambda s: C(s)),
